(i) ultra-narrowband networks have a larger range than wideband networks; (ii) ultra-narrowbands are more sensitive to interference than wideband networks, (iii) the range of a wideband network is less sensitive to interference than that of an ultra-narrowband network, and (iv) the range of wideband networks can be increased significantly by adapting the frequency and modulation to the network load and size.

ultra narrowband networks are more suitable for large networks with high node density, while wideband networks are more efficient when nodes are sparsely distributed and the network is small.
